beats.vo: Last page, Lesson 12.1, Your balance sheet. Build a personal on-chain balance sheet and read the three numbers that matter: equity, LTV and liquidity runway. Keep that page on the desk. This lesson adds one picture: Design custody so that no single lost device, stolen key or mistaken signature can drain the bank.

Education only, not financial advice. Crypto and DeFi carry significant risk, including total loss of capital. This is general information. It does not consider your objectives, financial situation, or needs. Past or example results do not indicate future results. Consider independent advice. We do not sell or run a trading bot.
On-Chain Operator. Lesson 12.2, Custody architecture: vault, multisig and spending policies. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You already keep a journal and a kill rule. A balance sheet is that habit turned into accounts.
Scale Module 1's three wallets into a bank-grade setup: Tier.
2-of-3 hardware keys in separate locations.
Moves only to the Operating tier, to allowlisted addresses Operating.
Hardware wallet or a smart account with limits.

Refilled on schedule Smart-account features to use where available: Spending limits per day/week Allowlists (it can only send to addresses you pre-approved) Timelocks on large moves (a delay you can cancel if it wasn't you) Recovery paths agreed and tested in advance.

Work the example on paper. Vault: 2-of-3 multisig, with key A at home, key B in a safe-deposit box and key C with a trusted person or a professional co-signer. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
Work the example on paper. Losing any one key is survivable; stealing any one key is useless. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
Work the example on paper. Test it: move $10 through every path once a quarter. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Vault is multisig; keys in separate physical locations. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Operating tier has a daily limit. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Allowlist on vault outflows. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Quarterly recovery test done and logged. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
Check yourself. 1. Why 2-of-3 rather than 1-of-1? The answer: One key can be lost or stolen without losing the funds or giving an attacker control.
Check yourself. 2. What does a timelock buy you? The answer: Time to notice and cancel an unauthorised large move.
Check yourself. 3. Why test recovery with a small amount? The answer: A recovery plan you've never run is an assumption. Testing proves every key and path works.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to design custody so that no single lost device, stolen key or mistaken signature can drain the bank.
